price.per: token (CP alone: every unit at zero cost)
price.src: tools/hgi_sim/timing.py schedule(recs, POS, 'S2', cost_fn=0) on the G25 DS rank-0 program with T.rebuild_waits (the records and schedule throughput_budget prices): fetch_latency 160 + 64 B / 2 cyc streaming prefetch, decode 1 + 1 a 32 B chunk, addr 2, wait rule, dispatch / retire wires; without wait masks 17,214

measured.def: doorbell -> last dispatch, units always ready and retiring the next cycle, memory lane always ready (FAST)

exactness: HGI_SEQ_DIE PASS: all 3,923 dispatches (header, SUT, 7 effective descriptors, n sidebands) equal the HGI-1 v1.0 reference sequencer (tools/hgi_seq_vectors.Ref) and the completion token / status match; committed 43-case vectors also PASS on the same build (committed_vectors_b1.log)
mutant: MUT 9 (loader burst one sector longer than its contiguous run) FAIL: FATAL more than 48 ring sectors in flight (m9_f160.log)
notes: The CP-alone time is ~59.7 cycles a dispatch and does not move with the HBM latency (104 / 160), the loader burst (BURST 0 / 1), the wait masks, or unit readiness: the fetch lane is NOT the limit (17,008 sectors in 234k cycles, 48 in flight cap never binding); the sequencer's per-record decode / effective-address path is (ot_hgi_seq: word-serial decode + ONE radix-16 iterative multiplier per scaled descriptor term, up to 7 descriptors a record) vs the simulator's 1 + 1-a-chunk decode + 2-cycle address. In the full token (S2 566.8k / 543k cycles, ~137 unit cycles a record) most of it hides behind unit time; the e2e residual (audit hbm_ds_cp_dispatch 1.16 on DS L0) is the token-level exposure. Lane model: the bench's in-order memory lane (48 sectors in flight, FLAT cycles, i.e. <= 9.6 B/cyc at FLAT 160) is not binding at the 2.04 B/cyc the CP draws; the real loader kport / svc native path is not in this bench (its rate is the SVC / loader owners' bench).
